clauses.reason: The sole operative paragraph of Executive Order 6329 reads, in its operative part: "do approve the granting of the aforesaid application, such modification and amendment to take effect one week from the date hereof, unless good cause to the contrary is shown to the Administrator before that time, and do order that the final approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Ship Building and Ship Repairing Industry contained in my Executive Order dated July 26, 1933, is hereby modified to the foregoing effect". The order approves an amendment of the Ship Building and Ship Repairing code (new Section 8(a), designating an industry committee as a planning and fair practice agency) and modifies the approval of that code in the order of July 26, 1933. The modification takes effect "one week from the date hereof, unless good cause to the contrary is shown to the Administrator before that time", that is October 17, 1933; this is a commencement condition, not an end, and no held record shows good cause shown. The amendment states no period or until-date. The committee provision, including the four members without vote appointed by the President, is part of the code text as amended and operates only through the code. The approval was code-dependent: under section 3(b) of the Act the approved provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under section 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under section 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor, so the approval operated only through section 3. Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval, so the approval ceased to operate on June 14, 1935. No held record shows the amendment cancelled, suspended or superseded before June 14, 1935 (the order of July 26, 1933 that it modifies is a different order and is not an end of this amendment). June 16, 1935 is not an end date: section 1 of the same resolution replaced the original two-year expiry of Title I with April 1, 1936, and nothing in the resolution defers section 2. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not as an end date.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 6329 (October 10, 1933) approves an amendment of the Code of Fair Competition for the Ship Building and Ship Repairing Industry under Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. The held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; Common Crawl capture 2025-12-07T01:24:05Z); the standing note applies: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved. The order approves one code amendment, taking effect one week after October 10, 1933 unless good cause were shown, and modifies the July 26, 1933 approval accordingly. Because each command is dependent on the code and no held record shows an earlier end, the first end is the statutory repeal of the code approval and enforcement provisions by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, effective June 14, 1935. Schechter, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; that is recorded as a validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not as an end date, because the judgment cancelled no approval. The antitrust-exemption proviso of the resolution is not settled by the held text for past action; whatever survives is an accrued effect, not continued operation of the approval.

United States, 295 U.S. 495, held the Live Poultry Code provisions in question invalid and reversed the conviction; recorded as the validity characterization of every section 3 approval, not as an end of this approval, because the judgment did not cancel or withdraw this order.

source_notes.reason: The opinion of the Court states: "We think that the code-making authority thus conferred is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power." The holding reaches section 3 approvals generally and is recorded as validity context only.
